en: An inclined plane like a ramp reduces the effort force needed to lift a heavy box by increasing the distance over which the force is applied.
Applying rubber treads to bicycle tires increases friction between the tire and the wet road, preventing the wheel from slipping during motion.
Earth's gravity pulls a dropped apple downward because every object with mass exerts an invisible attractive force on other objects.
Wrapping a copper wire around an iron nail and connecting it to a battery creates an electromagnet that attracts paperclips.
Rubbing a balloon on your hair transfers electrons to the balloon, giving it a negative charge that attracts neutral pieces of paper.
Light bends when passing from air into water because it slows down, making a pencil in a glass look broken.
Striking a drum vibrates its surface, pushing nearby air molecules to create sound waves that travel to your ear.
Heating one end of a metal spoon causes its atoms to vibrate faster, transferring thermal energy to the cooler handle through conduction.
Releasing a stretched rubber band converts its stored elastic potential energy into kinetic energy, causing it to snap forward rapidly.
Pushing down on the long end of a seesaw lever multiplies your force, lifting a heavier child on the short end.
The Sun heats the Earth through radiation by emitting electromagnetic waves that travel through empty space without needing physical matter.
Closing a switch completes an electrical circuit, allowing electrons to flow from the battery through the wire to light the bulb.
